questions.description: The program builds an ArrayList and then calls the two-argument add at index 1. What does the println print?

questions.title: Snippet: remove(int) Works by Index
questions.description: The program calls list.remove(1) on an ArrayList of Integers. Remember that remove(int) removes the element stored at that index, not the element equal to that value. What does the println print?

questions.title: Snippet: Autoboxed Integers in a HashSet
questions.description: The int literals are autoboxed into Integer objects when they are added to the HashSet, and a HashSet stores each distinct value only once. What does the program print?
questions.Option1: It throws an exception because 100 was added twice

questions.title: Snippet: HashSet add Returns a Boolean
questions.description: The program adds the same string twice and captures both return values of add. What does the println print?

questions.title: Fail-Fast Iterator Behaviour
questions.description: While iterating an ArrayList with an Iterator, the code calls list.remove(0) directly on the list instead of it.remove(). What is the expected behaviour?
questions.Option1: The Iterator silently skips one element and keeps going
questions.Option2: The next call to it.next() throws ConcurrentModificationException
questions.Option3: The list is copied automatically and iteration continues normally
questions.Option4: The code does not compile because remove is not allowed inside a loop

questions.title: Choosing a Sorted Set
questions.description: You need a set of names that automatically keeps them sorted in ascending order no matter what order they arrive in. Which implementation fits best?

questions.title: Snippet: Second remove Without next
questions.description: The program calls it.remove() twice with no intervening it.next() call. The Iterator contract forbids remove unless next has been called since the last remove. What happens?
questions.Option1: It removes the element 2 as well

questions.title: Snippet: List Remove During Iteration
questions.description: The loop removes an element directly from the list while the Iterator is still active; the next it.next() detects the modification. What happens when the program runs?
questions.Option2: It prints done once and removes every occurrence of 2
questions.Option3: It throws ConcurrentModificationException on the next it.next() call
questions.Option4: It throws IllegalStateException immediately at list.remove

questions.title: Snippet: set Returns the Old Element
questions.description: The program calls list.set(0, 9), which replaces the element at index 0 and returns the element that was stored there before. What does the println print?

questions.title: HashSet Internals
questions.description: Internally, the java.util.HashSet class stores its elements with the help of which structure?
questions.Option3: A LinkedList that preserves insertion order
questions.Option4: An internal HashMap instance where elements become keys
